phase: 10 (Phases D/G of autonomy: quality and governance)
completed_milestone: Phase A (the clock, fault classes, provider retries, the watchdog), Phase B/C (per-channel publish policy, the serial filmed in-run, captions and loudness measured), Phases E/F (a film's cost estimated and held before it is made, prices the Owner's alone, a failed render costed, a token ceiling with the Accountant's letter; the studio's own page discovery, a search engine filtered to the allowlist, the research health report in the preflight) and Phases D/G (2026-09-18: a picture gate and a character gate that certify only what they measured; the Character Bible's five reference slots filled by an Owner-triggered route; one approved alternative vendor per purpose per scene; the autonomy mode as a column, a versioned command and a tier gate the day asks before every stage, every paid film and every upload); Phase D/G closed the same day (2026-09-18: the Owner answers an approval and the day spends the answer once, migration 0044_approval_answered keying a request by the action and the film; his own render and quality control read a film the way the day reads it; Runway can be handed a character's reference; and a governance panel exists in frontend/src, unbuilt)
active_task: Phase D/G closed (2026-09-18): GET /api/v1/owner/approvals and POST /api/v1/owner/approvals/decision let the Owner answer a request that is keyed by the action and the film it is about; the answer is read inside may_act's SUPERVISED T3 branch after the stop, T4 and safe mode, and consumed before the act it authorises, so it converts 'he must be asked' into 'allowed, once' and never a refusal into a pass; both evaluate_media_qc call sites and start_render in media/router.py pass what the daily run passes; RunwayImageAdapter sends referenceImages on text_to_image; and frontend/src holds a governance panel for the mode, the approvals and the reference-set slots
next_task: The Owner's own acts, which no agent may perform: run scripts/bootstrap.py against the live database (0039, 0040, 0043, then 0044; main.py pins 0044_approval_answered), run npm run build --prefix frontend so the governance panel exists for him, answer the first approval a SUPERVISED day leaves him, produce the character reference sets (POST /media/characters/{id}/reference-set), choose the autonomy mode (POST /api/v1/owner/autonomy-mode), approve any fallback vendors, and the earlier list that is still his: his per-million prices, the budgets and the per-channel publish policy. Still unwritten in code: a letter telling him something is waiting; a way to withdraw a yes before it is spent; approval_expires_after_hours as a config key rather than a module constant now carrying three meanings; the Accountant's reconciliation of ESTIMATED rows against a vendor's invoice

known_blockers: No vision model has ever answered the picture check, here or anywhere: every test fakes the provider at its transport by the Owner's rule of 2026-09-17, and seed_initial_workforce seeds no vision-capable model (the Director's glm-5.3 declares completion, thinking and tools and no vision), so picture_qc and character_drift_qc will report NOT_APPLICABLE with their reason on the live studio until the provider catalogue sync records a vision-capable model on an employee

The Character Bible's five reference slots are empty on every studio that has ever run: POST /media/characters/{id}/reference-set fills them with real files but spends image credits, so it is the Owner's act and no stage of the day calls it; until he runs it, a character whose look is locked and has no readable reference refuses its film rather than having a face invented

No real render has gone through the second vendor, through OpenAI's /v1/images/edits multipart body or through Runway's referenceImages field: a studio whose Owner has approved no alternative has a chain of one, which is every studio today, REFERENCE_IMAGE_VERIFIED is False on both adapters until an Owner-approved run has drawn a scene that way, and the size of an inline reference is not checked because Runway's published data-URI limit was not read — a sheet too large will come back as a vendor refusal on the first live run, not as a silent truncation

No approval has ever been answered by a real Owner through the real route against a real database: since 2026-09-18 GET /api/v1/owner/approvals lists what waits and POST /api/v1/owner/approvals/decision answers it once, the request is keyed by the action and the film (subject, migration 0044), the yes is consumed before the act it authorises and owner_approval_request is in maintenance.HISTORY_TABLES — but every measurement is against the test engine with every provider faked, and 0044 has been walked from an empty database by every test in the run and never against data/studio.db

The Owner is not told that something is waiting: a SUPERVISED day records one approval request per film and the run record carries the approval id, but no letter and no notification is written, so the list is seen only by someone who opens the panel; and an approval cannot be withdrawn once given — the stop is the only way to hold a film back after a yes

The factual storyboard writes character_ids_json=[] (only serial_storyboard.py fills it), so on a factual film the character gate records that no scene lists a character rather than passing; and the Director is not told what quality control saw, because gather_facts filters the QC report to keys starting with 'measured'

51's department-scoped autonomy is not implemented: owner_policy.autonomy_mode is one global mode, and a per-department override needs the Owner's department list first. 51's acceptance criteria and burn-in are not checked either and cannot be from this database, so change_autonomy_mode names them in its refusal instead

The governance panel is written and not built: frontend/src/governance.js holds the judgements (14 tests) and main.js renders the autonomy mode, the approvals list and the Character Bible's reference-set chips, but frontend/dist was deliberately not rebuilt, so the Owner sees none of it until npm run build --prefix frontend; the screens themselves have no test because main.js touches the document at import, the refusal card sends no note although the command accepts one, and nothing yet renders the preflight's third severity (INFORMATIONAL), which must never be shown as a failure

The daily job is seeded dormant and stays so until the Owner's recorded activation (workflow.job_activated); no daily run has been queued by anyone since Phase A, by the Owner's rule that video generation costs money and happens only when everything is proven

No real day has run with both channels bound: the per-channel publish policy, the serial's routing to OFFICE_SERIAL, publishAt and videos.update were exercised only against faked providers and transports

director_may_approve_episodes defaults to false on every channel, so until the Owner grants it (POST /api/v1/publishing/channels/{id}/publish-policy) a Director's PASS leaves the episode DRAFT for the Owner and the serial produces no storyboard on its own
Today's log is still closed at the end of the run, so a date whose run completes is frozen at the run's hour; a full-day log for every date needs that close moved
No frontend screen sets the publish policy or the Director's leave, and the scheduler panel does not yet read run_at_local; the API carries both
The seeded Character Bibles carry no voice binding and the assembler synthesises one voice per scene, so every serial scene is the narrator until the Owner binds voices

The live database is still at 0038: migrations 0039 (pricing and reservations), 0040 (research sources), 0043 (autonomy mode and the approval request) and 0044 (the subject a request is about and the Owner's answer on the row) chain in that order — 0041 and 0042 were reserved in Phase D/G and neither was needed — and main.py pins 0044_approval_answered, so scripts/bootstrap.py must be run by the Owner before the server starts on this version

No budget and no price are set on the live studio: budgets are the Owner's alone (PUT /economy/budget) and a price enters the books only through PUT /economy/prices, so until he types them a reservation holds a plan priced from settings and the public ElevenLabs figure, and nothing refuses a day that has no budget

The Owner has typed no price, so every agent_run still records cost_vr NULL and the Accountant reports unpriced_agent_runs: the lookups are wired into all four construction sites and bootstrap seeds the one DOCUMENTED ElevenLabs figure, which makes a cost computable, not known. Ollama Cloud is deliberately never seeded

A vendor's invoice is never reconciled against the studio's estimates: the provenance vocabulary (QUOTED, BILLED) exists and no function matches a bill to the ESTIMATED rows of one render, so a render both estimated and later billed would be counted twice by the period's budget

No search engine is connected, so the studio can only find pages through the search addresses its authorised sites carry; the routes, the reason codes and the BLOCKED_BUDGET label exist in source, but frontend/dist is not rebuilt, so the served page still carries the old bundle

The script-only heuristic and the OpenSearch discovery are proven on fixture HTML modelled on the hosts that failed, not on live pages (no test may open a socket); the first weekly retest on the live database is the measurement

APPROVAL_EXPIRES_AFTER_HOURS = 24 is still a module constant in backend/app/services.py and now decides three things rather than one: how long an unanswered question stands, how long a refusal stops the studio asking again, and how long a yes can still be spent. Lifting it into config.py means naming all three meanings to the Owner

The Owner's manual quality control can now spend tokens: POST /media/qc/{identifier} makes the same single vision call per film the day makes and cuts frames with ffmpeg inside the request, metered only by the day's token ceiling and cached nowhere, because caching a measurement is how a gate starts certifying what it did not measure this time
